question: How many rows does an attribute edit need, and does the WDD vote order the rows better than a naive global order or a random one?
design: same models; k = 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32 first rows negated; orders: WDD vote (rows among any level's top ten, by best share), naive global (normalized activation difference over all MLP rows of blocks 0..L), three random; held-out flips by starting pole and wikitext KL.
smoke: Qwen2.5-0.5B, k to 8: best flips summed over poles WDD/naive/random gender 1.00/0.78/0.00, generation 0.25/0.00/0.00, number 1.00/0.40/0.10, polarity 0.00/0.00/0.00.

D1.text: at its best dose the WDD order flips at least 0.3 (summed over the two starting poles) for at least three of the four attributes

D2.text: averaged over doses, the WDD order flips more than the naive global order for at least three of the four attributes

D3.text: random orders flip at most 0.1 (summed over poles) at every dose for every attribute

D4.text: at the largest WDD dose, flips from the marked pole are at least three times those from the unmarked pole, for every attribute
